summary: Markets are broadly risk-on following a Democratic sweep of Congress in the midterm elections, with investors cheering the prospect of divided government reducing the likelihood of disruptive policy shocks under the Trump administration. The midterm results are the dominant macro catalyst, shifting expectations around U.S. foreign policy, energy regulation, and trade, with a Democratic-controlled Congress now positioned to constrain executive action on tariffs and military escalation. Oil prices slumped sharply as the election outcome raised bets on a de-escalation of the Iran conflict, while Home Depot extended its monthlong 25% rally on optimism around a more stable policy environment, and the AI trade saw a notable internal rotation as investors reassess which names benefit under the new political landscape. Key risks investors are monitoring include residual Iran geopolitical uncertainty — underscored by fresh U.S. sanctions on Indian and Turkish firms aiding Tehran — potential shifts in U.S. support for Israel, and the evolving trajectory of energy policy under a Democratic Congress that could pressure fossil fuel sectors. In the near term, the post-election rally appears likely to continue in rate-sensitive and consumer-facing sectors, though elevated geopolitical volatility and policy uncertainty around Iran and Middle East dynamics could introduce sharp reversals, particularly in energy and defense-linked equities.
